clue.text: Kid one in a kind of dance

indicators.note: in says the word for one is placed inside the dance word

parts.note: a barn dance is a country dance, so barn names a kind of dance
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A child is taking part in some sort of dance.
explanation.walkthrough: BAIRN is the Scottish and northern English word for a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for a young child, the Scots one and the everyday one.

clue.text: Lacking spirit, it may be barred

definitions.text: Lacking spirit, it may be barred

parts.words: Lacking spirit, it may be barred
parts.note: read as a place licensed to sell only ale, with no spirits, yet still having a bar

explanation.surface: Something dispirited might be banned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lacking spirit' looks like gloom and 'barred' like banned; in fact an old licence let such a pub sell beer but not spirits, and it has a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a pub was licensed for ale and beer only, with no spirits served.

clue.text: Unfit, you get to sleep in it

indicators.note: in places the word for sleep inside the word it

parts.note: taken as written
a nap is a short sleep

explanation.surface: Someone told they are not fit enough can rest inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means unsuitable or not fitting the purpose.

clue.text: Unbridled pony — these novices!

indicators.note: unbridled means unrestrained and wild, so the letters run loose

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Beginners exclaim at a horse without its bridle.
explanation.definitionFit: A neophyte is a beginner or new convert.

clue.text: Overshadow a stupid class

parts.note: dumb is slang for stupid
rate means class or grade, as in first-rate

explanation.surface: A dim set of pupils is put in the shade.
explanation.definitionFit: To adumbrate can mean to cast a shadow over, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Lady in a wicked environment is embarrassed

indicators.note: in, with environment, puts the lady inside the surrounding words

parts.note: bad means wicked
she is the pronoun for a lady

explanation.surface: A woman finds herself red-faced among bad company.
explanation.definitionFit: Abashed means made ashamed or self-conscious.

clue.text: Overturned — but finished up on top (25)

indicators.note: in a down clue, on top puts the word up above the word for finished

parts.note: ended means finished

explanation.surface: Something tipped over, yet came out ahead in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Something upended has been turned upside down or tipped on end.

clue.text: Move to name one name coming up

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: e.g. means for example, to name one
to dub is to name

explanation.surface: An instruction to shift so as to name one person after another.
explanation.definitionFit: To budge is to move or shift slightly.

clue.text: It's a long article ruined — he seeks agreements

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: ruined says the letters are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: the contraction of it is, letters I T S

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a lengthy piece of writing has been spoilt.
explanation.definitionFit: An analogist is one who reasons by analogy, looking for correspondences between things.

clue.text: Marner's Mary Ann

parts.note: read as the real surname of the woman who wrote Silas Marner, Mary Ann, pen name George Eliot

explanation.surface: Asking after a character named Mary Ann in the novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Mary Ann is not in the novel; Silas Marner's author George Eliot was the pen name of Mary Ann Evans.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian novelist known as George Eliot was born with this surname.

clue.text: Vanish with a girl to waffle about love

parts.note: Eva is a girl's name

indicators.note: about tells us the waffle word goes round the letter for love

parts.note: to prate is to talk on idly, to waffle
love is zero in tennis scores, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone disappears along with a girl so as to babble on about romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Water that evaporates disappears into the air, so to evaporate is to vanish.

clue.text: Daughter to drive — a tragedy, perhaps

parts.note: to ram is to drive or force something in

explanation.surface: A daughter takes the wheel, and disaster follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedy is one example of a play, a work of theatre.

clue.text: Get a lift from a jerk

definitions.meaning: to hitchhike, thumbing a ride from a passing driver

explanation.surface: Someone accepts a ride from an unpleasant man.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitchhiking means thumbing a ride, and a sudden tug or yank is also a hitch.

clue.text: These insectivores lay off filthy types

parts.note: to lay off a bet is to hedge it, betting the other way to limit losses
hogs are pigs, used of greedy or dirty people

explanation.surface: Some insect-eaters are told to keep away from grubby characters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay off' looks like an instruction to stop; it is the betting sense, to hedge.
explanation.definitionFit: These spiny garden animals feed mainly on insects, slugs and worms.

clue.text: Like a free girl, doesn't name the day

definitions.meaning: a girl not being dated by anyone is unattached
a document with no date written on it gives no day

explanation.surface: A single woman who won't fix a wedding date.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'name the day' is to fix a date for a wedding, which sharpens the picture of a free girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl nobody is taking out, and a letter bearing no date, are both described the same way.

clue.text: Like tatty books in the autumn of their lives?

definitions.text: Like tatty books in the autumn of their lives?

parts.words: Like tatty books in the autumn of their lives?
parts.note: read as worn books shedding their pages, as trees drop leaves in autumn

explanation.surface: Old battered books nearing the end of their days.
explanation.walkthrough: A book's pages are its leaves; trees that shed their leaves each autumn are described the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: Trees that lose their leaves seasonally carry this label, and tattered books shed pages, also called leaves.

clue.text: One who notes his life passing

definitions.text: One who notes his life passing

parts.words: One who notes his life passing
parts.note: read as someone who writes down each day's events as time goes by

explanation.surface: A person watching their life slip away.
explanation.definitionFit: A keeper of a daily journal records the events of each day as it goes.

clue.text: Abreast or — it may be so leading!

definitions.meaning: read as a long side, a team that is well ahead in a match

explanation.surface: Someone side by side with another wonders if they might be in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Being level and side by side is the same as being abreast, and split as a long side it describes a team well in the lead.

clue.text: To walk about certainly is dear to one's heart

indicators.note: about places the walking word round the word for certainly

parts.note: to tread is to walk
sure means certainly

explanation.surface: A stroll is undoubtedly something loved.
explanation.definitionFit: What is treasured is cherished and held dear.

clue.text: Duty many cut out

parts.note: excise is a tax or duty on goods
D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number

explanation.surface: Lots of people have been dropped from a tax.
explanation.definitionFit: To excise is to remove surgically or delete, the same as removing by cutting.

clue.text: Turns the lights down — the sodium variety on the Square

indicators.note: variety signals a different arrangement of the letters of sodium

parts.note: a T-square is a drawing tool, so T stands for square

explanation.surface: Sodium streetlamps on a town square are dimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: To dim out is to reduce lighting, as in a wartime blackout.

clue.text: Spoon? A job with the French!

parts.note: a post is a job or position
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone offered a job in France asks if it is just stirring things.
explanation.walkthrough: An apostle spoon is a traditional silver spoon with a figure of an apostle on the handle; the question mark marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A type of ornamental christening spoon is named after the twelve disciples carved on it.

clue.text: Made Bubbly

parts.note: read as given fizz by pumping gas into a liquid

explanation.surface: Someone has made champagne, or was made cheerful.
explanation.definitionFit: Water or drinks charged with gas become fizzy.

clue.text: Impulses in an actor are a form of madness

indicators.note: in says the impulses go inside the word for an actor

parts.note: a mummer is an actor in a traditional folk play
ids, in Freud, are the instinctive impulses of the mind

explanation.surface: An actor's urges amount to a kind of insanity.
explanation.definitionFit: Midsummer madness is a phrase for wild, foolish behaviour, supposedly brought on by the summer heat.

clue.text: The way with many for example

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner of doing something
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a large number

explanation.surface: The road taken by the crowd, to give an instance.
explanation.definitionFit: A model is a pattern or exemplar to copy.

clue.text: Total, so to speak

explanation.surface: A complete sum, as it were.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter means complete or absolute, and as a verb it means to say or voice.

clue.text: Note the girl's drink

parts.note: G is a musical note
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: Pointing out what the young woman is drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass of something is a drink, the container standing for its contents.

clue.text: Paddy sang — erratically in part

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An Irishman sang, though not always in tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paddy' looks like an Irishman; it is a fit of temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddy is a British informal word for a fit of temper.

clue.text: River — the same all round it Right?.

indicators.note: all round says the same word encloses the river letter

parts.note: do is short for ditto, meaning the same

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a river looks the same all around it.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'Right' is in French: droit means a right.
explanation.definitionFit: Droit is the French word, used in law, for an entitlement or legal claim.

clue.text: Where in France to start with a racing craft

parts.note: ou is French for where
to trigger something is to start it off

explanation.surface: A French place to begin with a racing boat.
explanation.definitionFit: An outrigger is a boat with a projecting float or rowlocks, used in rowing races.

clue.text: Salacity regarded as purified

parts.note: salacity is lewdness or lust
rated means regarded or considered

explanation.surface: Lewdness was treated as cleansing.
explanation.definitionFit: To lustrate is to purify ritually, by sacrifice or washing.

clue.text: Each colour like the com

parts.note: red is a colour

explanation.surface: Each ripe ear of corn has its own colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Corn that has formed its ears, the seed heads, is said to be in ear.
